newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JULY 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JULY 8.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The catastrophic fire near Thessaloniki over the weekend has signalled a bad start to the forest fire season, with the ashes of the Seih-Sou forest damning testament to lack of infrastructure and coordination.

--The government is considering reducing the number of days of treatment according to those insured with Social Security Foundation IKA in an effort to further cut costs. The issue will be discussed at a meeting attended by the national economy, health and labour ministers.

--New Turkish Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz appeared to adopt the hardline stance of his new deputy premier Bulent Ecevit on the Cyprus issue, undermining the talks to begin this week between Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash. Ecevit, a former prime minister, gave the order for Turkey to invade the island in 1974 and is known for his hawkish views on the issue.
--Sixty-four fires around the country have laid waste to some 60,000 stremmata and shown up the lack of preparation by services to combat fires.
--Thirteen employees of the Hellenic Telecommunications Organisation, OTE, will face minor charges over the signing of June 1994 contract for one million digital switches from Siemens and Intracom.

--Following election wins in Britain and France, it is time for European socialists to forge a new progressive road ahead, European Commissioner Christos Papoutsis says. A far-seeing policy on employment and social solidarity - which can be implemented - is needed.
--There are calls for Agriculture Minister Stephanos Tzoumakas's resignation, because his legal reforms have allegedly encourage arsonists and fire bugs.
--A 19-year-old model from Athens was last night selected as the first Greek Playmate of the Year.

--There may a compromise in the wings of 'social dialogue' between government, unions and employers: there are reports that unionists may accept deregulated working hours and less overtime in return for a 35-hour working week without any cut in pay. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
